t.1.131.1: Then King Duryodhana, together with his younger brothers, gradually won over all those subjects by gifts of wealth and marks of honor.
t.1.131.2: Then certain skilled counselors, set to the task by Dhṛtarāṣṭra, spoke of Vāraṇāvata as a delightful city.
t.1.131.3: This very great festival of Paśupati, the most delightful on earth, has begun in the city of Vāraṇāvata.
t.1.131.4: "…in a land strewn with every kind of jewel, a region delightful to men." In this way, at Dhṛtarāṣṭra's bidding, they spread such talk.
t.1.131.5: O king, as the delightful city of Vāraṇāvata was being described in this way, the sons of Pāṇḍu conceived the wish to go there.
t.1.131.6: But when the king thought, "Their curiosity has been aroused," then the son of Ambikā spoke to them, the Pāṇḍavas.
t.1.131.7: These men of mine constantly tell me, again and again, that the city of Vāraṇāvata is the most delightful in the world.
t.1.131.9: Give jewels to the brāhmaṇas and to the singers everywhere, as much as they desire, radiant like the gods.
t.1.131.8: My dear sons, if you think it fitting, then together with your companions and your retinue, go and enjoy the festival at Vāraṇāvata, sporting like the immortals.
t.1.131.10: Having thus enjoyed yourselves for some time and experienced the highest delight, you will return happily once more to this Hāstinapura.
t.1.131.11: Yudhiṣṭhira, perceiving that wish of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and his own lack of allies, replied to him, "So be it."
t.1.131.12: Then Bhīṣma of great wisdom, and Vidura of lofty mind, and Droṇa, and Bāhlika too, and Somadatta the Kaurava…
t.1.131.14: Father, at the command of Dhṛtarāṣṭra we shall dwell with our followers in the delightful city of Vāraṇāvata, crowded with people.
t.1.131.13: Then Yudhiṣṭhira softly spoke these sorrowful words to Kṛpa, to the teacher's son, and to the illustrious Gāndhārī.
t.1.131.15: All of you, with gladdened minds, utter auspicious words; no evil will overpower us who have been strengthened by your blessings.
t.1.131.16: Thus addressed by the son of Pāṇḍu, all those Kauravas, their faces brightening, approached the Pāṇḍavas.
t.1.131.18: Then the Pāṇḍavas, having had the rites for their well-being performed for the gaining of the kingdom, and having done all that had to be done, set out for Vāraṇāvata.
t.1.131.17: May there always be well-being for you on the road, and from all beings in every way; and may nothing inauspicious befall you from any quarter, O sons of Pāṇḍu.
